gaps.sentence: I ___ have said that — I apologised immediately.
gaps.explanation: 'Shouldn't have' expresses regret about a past action: shouldn't have.

gaps.sentence: There ___ be a supervisor present when students use the lab.
Students ___ to hand in essays by Friday at the latest.
gaps.hint: ought to takes the full infinitive
gaps.explanation: 'Ought to' takes the full infinitive, so only 'ought' fits before 'to': ought.

gaps.sentence: If you want a refund, you ___ keep the receipt — no receipt, no refund.
gaps.hint: a necessity that applies in the future
gaps.explanation: Future necessity uses 'will have to': will have to keep.

gaps.sentence: You ___ decide now — take your time and think it over.
gaps.explanation: 'Needn't' removes the obligation to act immediately: needn't decide.

gaps.sentence: You ___ not be so hard on yourself — everyone makes mistakes.
gaps.explanation: 'Should not' gives gentle advice against something: should not be.

gaps.sentence: It was careless of her — she ___ have prepared more thoroughly for the interview.
gaps.explanation: 'Should have' criticizes a failure to act properly: should have prepared.

gaps.sentence: I ___ rather not comment until the investigation is over.
gaps.hint: a polite refusal with would rather not
gaps.explanation: 'Would rather not' declines politely: would rather not.
